headers.$comment: Hashed filenames are content-addressed, so they can never go stale — cache them for a year and skip revalidation entirely. This is where most repeat-visit latency goes.

The service worker is the one file that must NEVER be cached. It is not content-hashed, so a cached copy pins every returning visitor to the build that installed it — they would stop receiving updates permanently, and no redeploy could reach them.
Same reasoning: the manifest and the registration shim are unhashed.
index.html is the entry point every navigation resolves to; caching it would serve an old asset manifest.
Icons are stable but not hashed — a week is a reasonable middle ground.
Baseline security headers. No CSP yet: MUI/Emotion inject runtime styles, so a correct policy needs a nonce pipeline rather than a guessed header that breaks the app.

rewrites.$comment: SPA fallback. Vercel serves a matching static file first, so this only catches client-side routes like /org/challenges/:id.
